newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Council gives up trying for unity on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Council gives up trying for unity on Iraq.

text.p: Britain on Friday gave up on a Security Council resolution criticising Iraq for its offensive in Kurdish provinces, mainly because of Russian opposition.

"Consideration of a resolution on Iraq has ceased because the British have said that while their text remains on the table they have ceased consultation on it," U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright told reporters. "We consider that an unfortunate result because there was clearly broad support for a resolution that criticised the Iraqis for the action they have taken."

"It shows that sometimes the council is not the most effective way to deal with this," Albright said. "We stand by what the United States did to deal with the problem in the northern governorates and it's just unfortunate that at this stage the council was not able to speak on the subject."

The deadlock illustrated the crumbling of the coalition that backed Washington in the 1991 Gulf War, with the United States coming under increasing criticism for firing cruise missiles against Iraq and claiming it had U.N. authorisation to do so. Britain supported the U.S. action but failed in its attempt to rally council members.

Russia opposed and threatened to veto the resolution, which was watered down considerably from the original in criticising Iraq for going into the Kurdish north. China agreed with Russia and France had reservations, as did Egypt and Indonesia.
Russia argued that the resolution was an attempt to give legal underpinnings to U.S. military actions against Iraq by not mentioning any of the cruise missile attacks.
